newsitem.title: UK: Oil rally pauses with signs of milder U.S. weather.
newsitem.headline: Oil rally pauses with signs of milder U.S. weather.

text.p: World oil prices paused for breath on Friday as traders took stock of this autumn's giddy climb and amid signs of some respite in the deepening gloom of winter in the U.S.
World benchmark Brent crude futures for January were valued at $23.45 per barrel at 1640 GMT, 15 cents down on the day and still well over $1 below October's six-year high of $25.06.
"I think this is more of a pause than anything else," said Tim Holmes of MeesPierson derivatives.
Fresh news of larger-than-expected supplies of North Sea oil in December also helped take a little of the shine off what has otherwise been a ferocious autumn rally.
Daily crude loadings from the North Sea's eight main export systems should rise by nearly two percent in December, latest schedules showed.

But at the heart of the oil price rally lies a longer-term and widespread fear that stocks of crude and refined oil products are short, particularly in the U.S., and that a repeat of last year's bitter winter could provoke a scramble to buy scarce barrels.
Traders feel that low inventories, particularly of heating oil or distillates, will maintain this year's prices at least at levels which are on average $3 a barrel above those of last year.
"Crude is showing fairly good supply in the North Sea, but to a large extent the recent strength has been heating oil and that still looks pretty good," Holmes said.
Latest data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) revealed another weekly fall in stocks of crude and refined products.

U.S. stocks of heating oil, which have formed the backbone of the recent rally, are over 10 percent lower than at this time last year. Almost all of this shortfall was concentrated in the key heating oil consuming region of the northeast, the data showed.
The trend was mirrored in Europe, where distillate stocks at the end of October were 22 million barrels below last year, according to the Euroilstock Foundation.

"In the U.S., things are also expected to warm up towards the middle of next week and that is a reason for not getting too carried away. But from the statistics we can see it still looks fairly constructive," Holmes said.
While independent forecaster Weather Services Corp predicts temperatures near normal for much of the United States over the coming week.
